stem.en: Kabir builds a five-carbon chain, then rotates it and submits it again as a second isomer. The bench refuses. Why?

text.en: Rotating a molecule does not change which atom is bonded to which. It is the same molecule seen from another side. An isomer needs a different set of connections.

feedback.en: Looking different on screen is not being different. Spin any object and it looks different; it is still one object.

text.en: Five carbons only have one isomer.

feedback.en: There are three. Two of them have branches. Rotating the chain finds none of them.

text.en: You can only submit each shape once.

feedback.en: The rule is nature's. Two drawings are the same molecule if every atom has the same neighbours in both.

explanation.en: Ask, for every atom, who its neighbours are. If the answer matches, it is the same molecule, whatever angle you drew it from.
